steps.code:
# Filter the data to only include brands with at least 10 hotels
df_final = df_filtered[df_filtered['brand_name'].isin(brands_with_10_plus)].copy()

print(f"Hotels from brands with at least 10 hotels: {len(df_final)}")

# Calculate average star rating by brand
brand_avg_rating = df_final.groupby('brand_name')['star_rating'].agg(['mean', 'count']).reset_index()
brand_avg_rating.columns = ['brand_name', 'average_star_rating', 'hotel_count']

print("\nAverage star rating by brand (sorted by average rating):")
print(brand_avg_rating.sort_values('average_star_rating', ascending=False))

# Find the brand with highest average star rating
max_rating = brand_avg_rating['average_star_rating'].max()
print(f"\nHighest average star rating: {max_rating}")

# Get all brands with the highest average rating (in case of tie)
brands_with_max_rating = brand_avg_rating[brand_avg_rating['average_star_rating'] == max_rating]
print(f"\nBrands with highest average rating:")
print(brands_with_max_rating)

# If there is a tie, return the brand with the largest number of hotels
if len(brands_with_max_rating) > 1:
    print("\nThere is a tie. Selecting brand with largest number of hotels:")
    brand_with_highest_avg = brands_with_max_rating.loc[brands_with_max_rating['hotel_count'].idxmax(), 'brand_name']
    print(f"Brand with highest avg rating and most hotels: {brand_with_highest_avg}")
else:
    brand_with_highest_avg = brands_with_max_rating.iloc[0]['brand_name']
    print(f"Brand with highest average star rating: {brand_with_highest_avg}")

print(f"\nFinal answer: {brand_with_highest_avg}")
